title: The Singhs Build Ram Rauni with Their Own Hands

blocks.text: Once the site is chosen, the page becomes practical and communal. A foundation is laid near the sacred complex, and the fort begins not as a royal project but as a labor shared directly by the Khalsa itself.

The text stresses that Singhs themselves served as masons, diggers, and builders. Walls rise quickly, gates are prepared, and the work of defense is performed by the same hands that will soon be required to fight.

A surrounding watercourse helps give Ram Rauni its shape and name, while the enclosure gathers several hundred defenders into one protected camp. The page therefore turns a religious resolution into visible architecture and collective discipline.
